claims: NSCA distinguishes two-foot lateral line jumping from single-leg lateral line hopping.
{{canonicalName}} is the bilateral takeoff-and-landing identity; single-leg lateral hop-to-stick remains a separate definition.
Unilateral and bilateral landings are biomechanically different contracts.
Declare two-foot takeoff, lateral projection, two-foot landing, target, terminal hold, full reset, and no rebound.
Jump landing involves hip, knee, and ankle absorption with trunk and pelvis control.
Declare gluteals, quadriceps, hamstrings, plantar flexors, foot and ankle stabilizers, adductors, and trunk stabilizers.
Bilateral landing distributes the contact across two feet and remains distinct from same-leg landing.
Observe simultaneous takeoff, lateral projection, simultaneous whole-foot landing, foot-knee-hip alignment, quiet absorption, hold, and reset.
Unilateral and bilateral plyometric tasks have different training demands.
Score exact amplitude variants on exercise complexity and physical difficulty, with overall as their maximum and no skill-level label.
Landing mechanics change with unilateral versus bilateral support.
Track bilateral takeoff and landing contacts, lateral impulse, lower-leg and tendon loading, landing noise, alignment, hold, output decline, and recovery.
A visible line or target constrains lateral direction and distance.
Declare surface traction, footwear, high-contrast target, lateral and fall space, lighting, traffic, and coach sightline.
Landing feedback should target defined observable mechanics.
Use low quality contacts, full reset, and enough rest to preserve lateral distance, simultaneous landing, alignment, hold, and quiet contact.
Two-foot and one-foot line drills must be named and taught separately.
Cue both feet set, load, push sideways, land on both whole feet together, absorb, hold, and reset.
Landing feedback can target trunk, knee, foot, and contact errors.
Stop for pain, swelling, instability, unsafe surface or lane, target miss, split landing, loud or partial-foot contact, valgus, trunk loss, extra hop, failed hold, or output decline.
Bilateral plyometric tasks should retain their declared support contract.
Use low amplitude for landing control and greater distance early and fresh for output; do not convert a terminal stick into continuous hopping.
Athlete support should show both-foot start, direction, target, distance, both-foot landing, hold, and reset.
Offer shorter distance, wider zone, snap-down or step-to-stick rehearsal, fewer contacts, longer rest, and nonvideo instruction.
Coach support must distinguish bilateral and unilateral landing mechanics.
Expose direction, distance, target, dose, rest, contact budget, observation angle, contact symmetry, alignment, hold, symptoms, and lane shutdown.
Landing tasks can be modified through feedback, progression, and environmental constraints.
Use a smaller distance, wider high-contrast zone, step-to-stick or snap-down regression, fewer contacts, longer recovery, and text or image instructions.
Two-foot versus one-foot support changes exercise identity, while line width and exact distance are modifiers.
Single-leg hops, contralateral bounds, continuous rebounds, hurdle entries, loaded landings, and reactive cues require separate review.
YouTube supports privacy-enhanced embedding through youtube-nocookie.com.

assessmentSummary.identity: A discrete bodyweight lateral jump from two feet to a simultaneous two-foot whole-foot landing, controlled terminal hold, and full reset.
currentCardFindings: The legacy card names direction and terminal stick but does not declare takeoff or landing laterality.
The existing low-amplitude source in the library explicitly describes a bilateral lateral jump and supplies lineage for the two-foot contract.
The completed single-leg card explicitly takes off and lands on the same declared leg, so support laterality is a deterministic identity boundary.
The display name should say bilateral lateral jump rather than rely on ambiguous hop terminology.
Five candidates have healthy oEmbed metadata only; no human media approval is created.
